steps.body: Once a group is counted, its number sticks. Asked again, the counter answers from memory — nothing changed, so the count still holds.
steps.narration: Once a group is counted, its number sticks. Asked again, the counter answers from memory — nothing changed, so the count still holds.

widget.prompt: You counted 6 shells. Show the answer again — without recounting.

commonCounts.feedback: Nothing was added; asking the question again does not grow the group.
Nothing was removed; the count of 6 still stands.

widget.missFeedback: The last count said 6, and the shells have not changed — show 6.
widget.successFeedback: Still six — the finished count keeps its answer while the group stays the same.

predict.prompt: Nothing changed since you counted 6. How many now?
predict.reveal: A count keeps its answer as long as the group is untouched.

cml.actionGoal: Pair each object with exactly one number and trust the last number said for kch recount.
invariants: A count pairs objects with number words one to one, and its last word names the whole group — which is why order, spacing, and arrangement can change without changing the answer for kch recount.
misconceptions: Skipping or double-counting an object, recounting when nothing changed, or believing a spread-out group holds more.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more object joined the group, what would the last counting word become?

widget.prompt: You counted 6 shells. Someone asks “how many?” Must you recount?

options.label: No — the last number of the count already answers it
options.feedback: Correct — the count's final number IS how many; nothing changed, so it still holds.

options.label: Yes — every question needs a fresh count
options.feedback: A finished count keeps its answer as long as the group is untouched.

options.label: Yes — shells are hard to count
options.feedback: Difficulty does not erase a finished count; 6 remains 6.

options.label: No — but the answer becomes 7
options.feedback: Asking the question does not add a shell; the count stays exactly 6.

widget.prompt: Start at 14 and count on 2. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 15 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 16.
17 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 2 hops from 14 to land on 16.

widget.successFeedback: 14 and 2 more is 16 — counting on continues the count instead of starting over.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 2 counts are needed to reach 16.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 2 numbers, on 16.

widget.prompt: Compare 4 and 4. Which statement is true?

options.label: They are equal
options.feedback: Correct — the same numeral names the same amount every time, so the two match exactly.

options.label: The first number is greater
options.feedback: Both numbers are 4, so neither one is greater than the other.

options.label: 4 is less than 4
options.feedback: A number cannot be less than itself; the two values are equal.

options.label: You cannot tell
options.feedback: You can tell at a glance — the numerals are identical, so the amounts are too.
